task.title: Behaviour-preserving refactor of kvparse.parser
task.statement: Refactor kvparse/parser.py without changing any behaviour. Two changes are requested. (1) parse_line(line) must be rewritten without the hand-rolled index loops: split the line at the first '=' with str.partition, strip the key and the value, raise ValueError when there is no '=' or the stripped key is empty, and remove one pair of matching surrounding quotes (both ends '"' or both ends "'") from a stripped value of length two or more; the function must not contain a 'while' loop. (2) Extract the detection of ignorable lines into a module-level function _is_ignorable(line) -> bool in kvparse/parser.py that returns True exactly when the stripped line is empty or starts with '#' or ';', and make parse use it. The observable behaviour of parse and parse_line must stay byte-for-byte identical for every str input: the same return values, the same exception types in the same situations (TypeError for non-string input to parse, ValueError for a malformed line), later duplicate keys still win, and quotes are removed only when the stripped value starts and ends with the same quote character (a value like '"x\'' keeps both characters; a lone '"' is kept). Exception messages are not prescribed. parse keeps raising TypeError for non-string input; what parse_line does with a non-string argument (for example a list or a mapping) is unspecified and must not be tested, because the required use of str.partition changes it. Keep the public names parse and parse_line exported from kvparse, do not modify the tests, and keep the existing suite passing.
acceptance_criteria: parse_line raises ValueError for '', 'novalue', ' = v', '   ', '=' and '\t= 1'.

parse behaviour unchanged: comments ('#' or ';' as the first non-blank character), blank lines and Windows line endings are handled as before; later duplicate keys win; parse('') == {}; parse('k = v') == {'k': 'v'}.
parse raises ValueError for a malformed line anywhere in the text and TypeError for non-string input (None, 3, a list, bytes).
kvparse.parser._is_ignorable exists, returns True for '   # c', '' and '\t; c', and False for 'a = 1' and 'a = # not a comment'.
The source of parse_line contains no 'while' loop and uses str.partition.
The existing tests in tests/ pass unchanged.
Unspecified, not to be tested: parse_line with a non-string argument.

spec.restated_task: Refactor kvparse/parser.py while preserving its defined string-input behavior: replace parse_line's manual scanning with partition at the first '=' and retain whitespace trimming, validation, and removal of exactly one matching surrounding quote pair; extract blank/comment-line detection into module-level _is_ignorable(line) -> bool and have parse use it. Exception messages and parse_line behavior for non-string arguments are outside the contract.

interface_contract.name: kvparse.parser.parse_line (also exported as kvparse.parse_line)
interface_contract.behavior: For a string argument, use str.partition via line.partition('=') to split at the first equals sign. Strip surrounding whitespace from the key and value using str.strip semantics. Require a separator and a nonempty stripped key. If the stripped value has length at least two and both endpoints are the same single or double quote character, remove exactly those endpoints without changing the interior. Return a two-element tuple of strings (key, value). Do not contain a while loop or retain manual index-scanning loops.
error_cases: ValueError: the portion before the first '=' is empty after stripping.
Non-string arguments are unspecified and must not be tested; exception messages are unspecified.

interface_contract.name: kvparse.parser.parse (also exported as kvparse.parse)
interface_contract.behavior: Validate input with the existing isinstance(text, str) rule. Iterate text.splitlines() in order, use _is_ignorable to skip blank and full-line comment lines, and pass each remaining raw line to parse_line. Return a dict mapping parsed keys to parsed values. Later occurrences overwrite earlier values for the same key; preserve existing dictionary insertion order. Empty or entirely ignorable input returns an empty dict. Do not treat inline '#' or ';' as comment delimiters.
error_cases: TypeError: text is not an instance of str, including None, integers, lists, and bytes.
ValueError: any non-ignorable line lacks '=' or has an empty stripped key; propagate the failure rather than returning partial results.

interface_contract.name: kvparse.parser._is_ignorable
interface_contract.behavior: Module-level helper for string lines. Return True exactly when line.strip() is empty or starts with '#' or ';'; otherwise return False. Return an actual bool. This helper need not be exported from kvparse.
error_cases: Non-string arguments are outside the specified contract.

acceptance_criteria: 1. parse_line('a=b') == ('a', 'b'), parse_line(' a = b ') == ('a', 'b'), parse_line('a==b') == ('a', '=b'), and parse_line('a = b = c') == ('a', 'b = c').
2. parse_line('a=') == ('a', '') and parse_line('a=   ') == ('a', ''); empty values are valid.
3. parse_line('q = "x"') == ('q', 'x'), parse_line("q = 'x'") == ('q', 'x'), parse_line("q = ''") == ('q', ''), and parse_line('q = ""') == ('q', '').
4. parse_line('q = "x\'') == ('q', '"x\'') and parse_line('q = "') == ('q', '"'). Likewise, reverse mismatched endpoints and a lone single quote remain unchanged after whitespace stripping.

5. parse_line('q = " spaced "') == ('q', ' spaced '), parse_line('k e y = v') == ('k e y', 'v'), and parse_line('u = "a" "b"') == ('u', 'a" "b'). Remove only one surrounding quote pair, including for nested matching quote pairs, and perform no escape processing or interior whitespace normalization.
6. parse_line raises ValueError for each of '', 'novalue', ' = v', '   ', '=', and '\t= 1'. Lines beginning with '#' or ';' receive no special treatment when passed directly to parse_line.

7. For string inputs, key/value trimming matches Python str.strip semantics, including Unicode whitespace. All remaining characters are preserved exactly. parse_line itself does not split input into lines.
9. parse ignores empty lines, whitespace-only lines, and lines whose first character after stripping is '#' or ';', even when such comments contain no '='. Entirely ignorable text yields {}.

10. parse preserves text.splitlines() behavior for LF, CRLF, CR, and other separators recognized by str.splitlines(), including trailing separators. For example, parse('a=1\r\nb=2\r\n') == {'a': '1', 'b': '2'}.
11. parse('a=1\nb=2\na=3') returns {'a': '3', 'b': '2'} with key iteration order ['a', 'b']; duplicate keys are determined after key stripping.
12. parse('a = # not a comment\nb = ; also a value') == {'a': '# not a comment', 'b': '; also a value'}.
13. A malformed non-ignorable line at the beginning, middle, or end of parse input raises ValueError, including when surrounded by valid assignments or comments.
14. parse raises TypeError for None, 3, [], and b'a=b', and retains the existing isinstance(text, str) input-validation rule.

15. _is_ignorable is available at kvparse.parser._is_ignorable and returns True for '   # c', '', '\t; c', and whitespace-only strings; it returns False for 'a = 1', 'a = # not a comment', and 'x; comment'.

16. Source inspection confirms parse_line calls partition('=') on the input string, contains no while loop, and replaces the manual index-scanning loops. Source inspection confirms _is_ignorable is module-level and parse uses it to decide which lines to skip.
17. from kvparse import parse, parse_line continues to work and exposes the corresponding functions from kvparse.parser.
18. Existing files under tests/ remain unchanged and the existing suite passes. Additional verification must not prescribe exception messages or test parse_line with non-string arguments.

Sealed and adversarial suites run one child process per test under a supervisor that never imports candidate code and is the first step of its branch; two verifier canaries detect blanket result forgery. A candidate can still forge its own result from inside a child after the nonce was read if it spares the canaries (the mutation gate and held-out tests are the structural detectors).

The repository's own suite and the held-out suite run after the sealed verification in their own branches. They are bound through the same supervisor only for unittest repositories whose tests are statically discoverable; otherwise they are parsed from console output and the gate is labelled evidence_class 'stdout'.

Model-written sealed and adversarial tests can be wrong; their failures block VERIFIED. An independent arbiter classifies each failure (implementation bug, test defect or contract dispute) and, for pure test defects, offers a corrected module. The correction counts only after mechanical validation (same test methods, only the failing tests' bodies changed, passes on the candidate, still fails on the unmodified base or is caught by a mutant, with every result structurally sound and bound to its nonce); the corrected gate is then re-run and the verdict re-derived from the gates. A sealed test that failed by assertion or by an exception, whatever its origin, is never overridden (only a test the supervisor killed at its timeout may be corrected). The classification itself remains a model judgement.

A mutant counts as killed only when a sealed test failed with an authentic child result under a structurally sound supervisor run; lost, forged, incomplete, non-isolated, crashed or timed-out runs are unknown and excluded from the mutation score, and `attest check` recomputes the classification from the raw results.

INFEASIBLE is recorded only when a witness program written by the contract auditor demonstrated the contradiction by running on the unmodified repository (exit code and output recorded); the witness's logic is the model's, its execution is not.
Grounding runs only when the specification names external references; sources are cited, not verified for correctness.
